hook_text: 8 stacks of chairs, 96 chairs. How many in a stack? Guess wrong on purpose and watch it fix itself.
clip_script: School hall in Mbombela. 96 chairs in 8 equal stacks. 8 times box equals 96. Do not know it? Guess. Try 10: 8 times 10 is 80. Too small, so go bigger. Try 13: 104. Too big, so go smaller. Try 12: 96. Got it, 12 chairs a stack. Every wrong guess pointed the way. Now the shortcut: undo. Times 8 is undone by divide by 8. 96 divided by 8 is 12. One step. Now the trap. Box minus 268 equals 457. Do not do 457 minus 268. Something was taken from the box and 457 is left, so put it back: 457 plus 268 is 725. Check: 725 minus 268 is 457. True. Always put the answer back in. The sentence tells you if you are right.
visual_style: Whiteboard balance scale with a box on one pan; guesses written in a column with arrows up and down; a chair stack growing to 12.
mood: Playful game of hot and cold.
pacing: Three fast guesses, the undo shortcut, the one trap, then the proof step.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and solve a missing-number sentence from your homework two ways.
